query: Which material can be used for enhanced catalytic activity and durability toward HER and HOR, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Alloying platinum (Pt) with nickel (Ni) will enhance catalytic activity and improve durability for hydrogen evolution (HER) and hydrogen oxidation (HOR) reactions, compared to pure Pt catalysts.
generation.material_initial_state: Commercial platinum on carbon (Pt/C) catalyst powder
generation.intervention: Synthesis of a Pt–Ni alloy catalyst by partial substitution of Pt with Ni in the metal sites
generation.conditions: Deposited on porous carbon electrodes; performance evaluated under typical electrochemical conditions for HER/HOR in acidic electrolyte solutions
generation.structural_mediator: Incorporation of Ni into Pt modifies the local electronic environment and changes the hydrogen adsorption energy on the catalyst surface
generation.mechanism: Electronic interaction between Pt and Ni weakens hydrogen binding, enhancing both adsorption–desorption kinetics and stability against dissolution
generation.predicted_outcome: Enhanced exchange current density and improved operational stability relative to pure Pt, likely on the order of tens of percent increase in catalytic activity
generation.baseline: Performance of unmodified commercial Pt/C measured under identical testing protocols
generation.boundary: Optimal Ni content depends on synthesis routes and may differ between HER and HOR; excessive Ni can reduce stability or block surface active sites
generation.uncertainty: Further investigation is needed to determine the long-term performance and durability in real device operating conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Compare HER and HOR kinetics of Pt–Ni alloy vs. unmodified Pt using rotating disk electrode measurements under identical operating conditions for a set timeframe (e.g. 1000 cycles). Analyze catalyst morphologies pre- and post-cycling to assess degradation.
measurements: Post-test characterization of catalyst microstructure by TEM/SEM/EDX
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Pt–Ni alloy does not exhibit measurably higher activity (lower overpotential or higher exchange current density) and reduced degradation compared to pure Pt under the same conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
